newsitem.title: USA: "The English Patient" tops Screen Actors' nominees.
newsitem.headline: "The English Patient" tops Screen Actors' nominees.

text.p: "The English Patient", the war drama starring Ralph Fiennes and Kristin Scott Thomas, topped the list of nominations for the Screen Actors' Guild awards on Thursday.

The film, Anthony Minghella's adaptation of Michael Ondaatje's Booker prize-winning novel, picked up four nominations while "The Birdcage", "Marvin's Room", "Jerry Maguire" and "Shine" each received three.

"Evita", the epic musical starring pop singer Madonna which won three Golden Globe awards last Sunday, was shut out. Madonna won the Golden Globe for best actress in a musical or comedy film in the title role, and has predicted she will get an Oscar nomination for the screen adaptation of the Andrew Lloyd Webber musical.
A nominating committee of 4,200 randomly chosen guild members selected the nominees and the guild's 86,000 members will decide the winners, which will be announced on Feb. 22.
Fiennes was nominated for a best leading actor award for his role in "The English Patient" and Scott Thomas was nominated for best performance by a leading actress.
Juliette Binoche was nominated in the best supporting actress category and the movie was also nominated for "outstanding performance by a cast".

Other nominations for best leading actor were Tom Cruise, who played an idealistic sports agent in "Jerry Maguire", and Woody Harrelson for "The People vs. Larry Flynt", the story of the controversial publisher of "Hustler" magazine.
Also nominated were Geoffrey Rush, who plays a mentally disturbed pianist in "Shine" and Billy Bob Thornton for "Sling Blade."

British actress Brenda Blethyn was nominated in the best leading actress category for playing a traumatized mother in "Secrets & Lies". Also nominated were Diane Keaton for "Marvin's Room", Frances McDormand for "Fargo" and Gena Rowlands for "Unhook the Stars".

Film legend Lauren Bacall, who played Barbra Streisand's possessive mother in "The Mirror has Two Faces", was among the nominees for best supporting actress. She won the Golden Globe for the role on Sunday.
On the television side, the comedy "Seinfeld" and police drama "NYPD Blue" each received four nominations, with "The X-Files", "3rd Rock from the Sun", "Frasier" and "ER" each receiving three.

The Golden Globes and other film awards are often viewed as barometers of the Oscars, Hollywood's highest honours, which are presented by the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences in March. The Oscar nominations will be announced next month.
